cells.tense: You're here, with both hands on what's arriving.
cells.verb: Tending what's growing with responsible care, holding two demands at once without choosing between them.
cells.place: At the threshold where what was outside is coming in — meeting it as it arrives, not after.
cells.ask: Offer what's arriving the honor of being noticed — say out loud what you're carrying for whom. When that lands, release comes on its own, completion rather than defeat.
cells.core:
You're tending something as it comes in, and you're doing it with both hands — not deciding which priority wins, but keeping both fed. What's arriving gets your care before it gets your judgment, and the care is deliberate. Nobody had to ask you to hold it.
The holding isn't costing you. That's the tell.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending what's arriving, both hands on it, and it isn't costing you.

cells.tense: You're already bracing for a harvest that hasn't been planted yet.
cells.verb: Tending ahead of the arrival — managing what hasn't come in, forcing care past the point where it feeds anything.
cells.place: At the threshold you've already crossed in your head, standing over what's still outside.
cells.ask: Let one thing finish — let an experience be fully processed before you reach for the next. Vision that flows from what you've actually lived is what you're after. When that lands, care stops exhausting you and starts holding without clutching.
cells.core:
You're out ahead of what's arriving — already arranging the next thing, the next season, the next load, before any of it has come through the door. The tending is real. The timing isn't. You've turned stewardship of what's here into management of what might be.
What's coming has nowhere to land because the landing zone is full of scaffolding.
cells.sheetLine: You're arranging what hasn't arrived yet, and it's crowding out what has.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that already closed behind you.
cells.verb: Not picking anything up — knowing there was something to tend and not reaching for it.
cells.place: Past the threshold and not entering, where what's been outside stays outside.
cells.ask: Keep hoping about one thing past the point where it's reasonable — not working at it, just refusing to let the aspiration die. Strength comes back through continued hoping. When that lands, what you cultivated starts radiating on its own — shining because it ripened, not because you pushed it.
cells.core:
Something was meant to be tended and you didn't pick it up. Not because it wasn't yours — because at some point the reaching stopped. The care is still in you. It's just not moving toward anything.
What's arriving waits at the door. You know it's there. You're not going.
cells.sheetLine: There's something to tend and your hands aren't on it.

cells.tense: You're already tending it and you're telling yourself it's tending you.
cells.verb: Stewarding what's entering, deciding which of two demands gets fed, and doing it without saying so.
cells.place: At the threshold you're already standing at, holding the door without calling it yours.
cells.ask: Let one thing you're carrying be seen — name the intent behind the tending, out loud, to one person. When it's witnessed, release comes as completion, not as quitting.
cells.core:
You're already deciding what gets carried and what doesn't — holding both demands right now, choosing how to keep them, and you talk about it as though the situation were doing the choosing. The tending is running. The claim on it isn't.
Nothing about what you're doing is passive. The naming is.
cells.sheetLine: You're choosing how this gets tended. You haven't said it's your choice.
